title: Convergence/exhaustiveness & separatedness of the $\aO$-slice tower (connective case)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (NEW): Convergence, exhaustiveness, and separatedness of the $\aO$-slice tower for connective spectra.**

The problem asks for a *slice filtration* and a characterization of the $\aO$-slice connectivity of a **connective** $G$-spectrum. A layer-by-layer characterization is vacuous unless the $\aO$-slice tower actually converges to $E$. This sub-lemma is logically independent of the *existence* of the tower (tracked in q5-27) and of the question "where is the connective hypothesis used" (q5-32); neither states or proves convergence/separatedness.

**To prove.** For bounded-below (connective) $E$:
$$\mathrm{holim}_n\, P^{\aO}_{\le n}E \;\simeq\; E,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \bigcap_{n}\tau^{\aO}_{\ge n}\big|_{\text{bdd below}} = 0\ \ (\text{separatedness}),$$
and the connecting maps assemble to the identity in the limit.

**Why it is genuine and load-bearing.** With an *incomplete* $\aO$ there are strictly fewer slice generators (only admissible norm cells $G_+\wedge_H S^{\mathbb R\cdot T}$, $T\in\aO(H)$), so a priori the slice-coconnective quotients can be "too large" and the tower could fail to separate. The multiplier in the connectivity estimate is $r_H=[H:\chi^{\aO}(H)]$ rather than $|H|$, and one must verify that $\min_H$ over the relevant range still $\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ so that the tower exhausts $E$.

**Suggested route.**
1. Forward estimate: $r_H\,\mathrm{gconn}(\Phi^H P^{\aO}_{\ge n}E)\ge n$ shows the $n$-coconnective cover becomes highly $\Phi^H$-connected as $n\to\infty$ for every relevant $H$.
2. Apply the connectivity-detection (conservativity) lemma for $\{\Phi^H\}$ on bounded-below spectra (see companion new issue) to the fiber of $E\to P^{\aO}_{\le n}E$ to conclude $\mathrm{holim}_n P^{\aO}_{\le n}E\simeq E$.
3. Mirror the HHR / Hill--Yarnall convergence argument with $|H|\rightsquigarrow r_H$, checking the bounded-below hypothesis is used exactly where geometric fixed points would otherwise fail to be jointly conservative.

References: HHR (Ann. of Math. 184, 2016) slice convergence; Hill--Yarnall (PAMS 146, 2018); Hill, *Slice filtration primer* (HHA 14, 2012).
